title: Polynomial resolutions remain resolutions under Tor-independent tensoring
statement: Let $A\to B$ and $A\to A'$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings, put $B'=B\otimes_A A'$ [def-weil-module-base-change], and let $P_\bullet\to B$ be a polynomial resolution in the precise sense of [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence]. Thus $P_n$ is a polynomial $A$-algebra surjecting onto $B$, and the alternating-face complex $s(P_\bullet)\to B[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism. If the canonical map $B\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'\to B'[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], where derived scalar extension is [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] transported to ordinary modules by [lem-trf-one-point-derived-ring-identification], then $P_\bullet\otimes_A A'\to B'$ is a polynomial resolution over $A'$, with its given tensor augmentation.

source.place: Tag 08QP (lemma-flat-base-change), proof identifying s(P) tensor A′ with the complex computing B tensor-derived A′; the resolution convention is Tag 08QI (remark-resolution).

proof.text: Put $C=s(P_\bullet)$ and let $q:C\to B[0]$ be the augmentation. The hypothesis and [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence] give that $q$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $C$ is zero in positive degrees. Choose the polynomial coordinates supplied by the polynomial-term hypothesis and apply [lem-trf-polynomial-simplicial-tensor-model]: every term of $C$ is flat, the base-changed simplicial algebra has polynomial terms and surjective augmentations, and there is an isomorphism $\phi:Q_{A'}(C\otimes_A A')\simeq Q_{A'}s(P'_\bullet)$ carrying the actual tensor augmentation to the given augmentation $q'$ of $P'_\bullet$.

source.place: Tag 08QP (lemma-flat-base-change), the free-module resolution s(P); Tag 08QI (remark-resolution), associated-complex convention.

proof.text: By Step 1, $C$ is bounded above by zero with flat terms and $q:C\to B[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Apply [lem-trf-flat-resolution-canonical-tensor-comparison] with $N=B$, bound $b=0$, and the transported universal derived pair occurring in the statement. It supplies an isomorphism $j_q:Q_{A'}(C\otimes_A A')\simeq B\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'$ with $\gamma_{B[0]}\circ j_q=Q_{A'}(q\otimes1)$. The hypothesis makes $\gamma_{B[0]}$ invertible, so $Q_{A'}(q\otimes1)$ is invertible.

source.place: Tag 08QP, final derived-to-ordinary comparison; naturality and computation in derived.tex Tags 05S9 and 06XN; ordinary module counit more-algebra.tex Tag 06Y6 (lemma-derived-base-change).

proof.text: The first step gives $Q_{A'}(q')\circ\phi=Q_{A'}(q\otimes1)$. Both $\phi$ and the right side are isomorphisms, hence so is $Q_{A'}(q')$. By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], each cohomology functor factors through localization. Applying it to the invertible $Q_{A'}(q')$ makes every $H^r(q')$ invertible; thus the specified $q'$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Its polynomial terms and degreewise surjective augmentation were established in the first step. These three conditions are exactly the polynomial-resolution criterion of [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence].

source.place: Tag 08QP, identity s(P) tensor A-prime = s(P tensor A-prime), including its augmentation.

proof_origin.place: Tag 08QP (lemma-flat-base-change), proof, expanded using Tag 08QI and the natural counit formula of derived.tex Tags 05S9/06XN. The one-object-site bridge is stated separately.
